pairs.why: Both chess tables have a solid pedestal on a base slab and two stools standing on the grass, all from one camera, so I can't find a build error in either.
B's armrests and X-legs clearly join the seat and back posts, while A's back posts and lower frame bars meet the seat ambiguously.
A's slim pillar and B's flared pedestal both hold their tops up, and every stool sits flat on the grass, so neither has a structural fault.
The two coiled ropes are almost identical: the tie, the whipped ends and the loop running into the coil read the same in both.
Both tables stand on square bases with stools beside them from a consistent camera, so I see nothing broken in either.
A hangs from a single clamp and stem into a yoke that pivots on both sides of the lamp, like the real card; B's yoke clamped straight to the truss also works, so this one is close.
B's yoke hangs from one clamp and pivots on both sides of the lamp, while A's square yoke reaches the small lamp on one side only and its other arm just ends on top of the body.
A's U-yoke pivots on both sides of the lamp body, while B's square yoke has a pivot on one side only and its other arm runs into the top of the long body.
